title: Very tame quotient is log regular
statement:
Let $D$ be an integral Noetherian scheme, let $(D,E)$ be a log regular pair, and let a finite group $G$ act on this pair admissibly, generically freely and very tamely. Suppose the finite scheme quotient $q:D\to Y=D/G$ exists with orbit-space topology and $\mathcal O_Y=(q_*\mathcal O_D)^G$. Then $Y$, with log structure $(q_*M_D)^G$, is fs log regular, its triviality locus is $Y\setminus q(E)$, and $(Y,q(E))$ is a log regular pair. Here $M_D$ is the divisorial log structure; the fs condition means admitting étale-local charts by finitely generated integral saturated monoids, as in [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

Here admissible means that each orbit is contained in an affine open; generically free means free on geometric points over a dense invariant open. An action on a pair preserves its closed subset and hence its divisorial log structure. The log regular pair and its geometric stalks are those of [def-trf-log-regular-pair].

At a geometric point $\bar c$, write $A=\mathcal O_{D,\bar c}$, $M$ for the divisorial log stalk, $\overline M=M/A^\times$, $I$ for the ideal generated by nonunit log sections, and $H$ for the stabilizer of the geometric point. Very tame means that $|H|$ is prime to the residue characteristic, $H$ acts trivially on $\overline M$, and $H$ acts trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$. In residue characteristic zero the prime-to-characteristic condition is void.

source.place: Expose VI Theorem 3.2 and Proposition 3.5(c), printed pp.73–75; VI 1.4 identifies the divisorial log structure; quotient-pair form explicitly used in IX 2.4, p.134.

proof.text: Put $N=(q_*M_D)^G$. Its structural map lands in $(q_*\mathcal O_D)^G=\mathcal O_Y$. An invariant log section mapping to a unit has its inverse as an invariant unit section, and every unit of $\mathcal O_Y$ gives such a section. Thus $N$ is a log structure. Apply [lem-per-finite-quotient-strict-local-invariants] to the given finite quotient: $Y$ is Noetherian, and for each geometric $\bar y$ and lift $\bar x$ we have $B=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}=A^H$ with $A=\mathcal O_{D,\bar x}$ finite over $B$ and $N_{\bar y}=M_{D,\bar x}^H$. The geometric fibre is an orbit: on an affine quotient, the invariant-ring quotient has transitive geometric fibres, as included in the finite-quotient comparison. The equality is for the geometric stabilizer $H$, not for the stabilizer of the underlying ordinary point.

source.place: VI paragraph after 3.5, and 3.7(b), opening reduction

proof.text: Fix these points and put $Q=\overline M_{D,\bar x}$. The log regular pair definition says $M_D$ is fs, $A/I$ is regular, and $\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}$, for the ideal $I$ generated by the nonunit log sections. Very tameness gives invertibility of $n=|H|$, triviality on $Q$, and triviality on $A/I$. Apply [lem-per-very-tame-equivariant-sharp-chart] to obtain a sharp chart $a:Q\to M_D$ with diagonal character $\chi$ and fixed roots of unity. In this chart $I=(a(q):q\ne0)$: the stalk is $Q\oplus A^\times$, and a section is a nonunit exactly when its $Q$-component is nonzero.

Apply [lem-per-very-tame-local-kummer-quotient] to $A,M_{D,\bar x},H,a,\chi$. Its finite-algebra hypothesis is Step 1, its invertible-order and trivial-stratum hypotheses are very tameness, and its diagonal chart is Step 2. It gives the sharp fs invariant chart $P=Q\cap L$, where $L$ is the kernel of all characters, $P^{\rm gp}=L\supseteq nQ^{\rm gp}$, and an isomorphism $B/J\simeq A/I$ with $J=(a(p):0\ne p\in P)B$. By Step 1 this is a chart of the actual invariant direct image $N$; its neighbourhood clause supplies an etale-local chart on $Y$, not merely a presentation of an abstract stalk. Applying this at every point proves that $N$ is fs.

source.place: VI 3.7(b), invariant chart, and beginning of 3.7(c), strata

proof.text:
The injection $B=A^H\hookrightarrow A$ is integral because $A$ is finite over $B$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral] and [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-dimension-equal] to get $\dim B=\dim A$. Since $L$ contains $nQ^{\rm gp}$, tensoring the inclusion with $\mathbf Q$ gives equality of rational spans, hence $\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp}=\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}$. Substitute the Step 2 dimension equality and the Step 3 stratum isomorphism:
$$\dim B=\dim A=\dim(A/I)+\operatorname{rank}Q^{\rm gp}=\dim(B/J)+\operatorname{rank}P^{\rm gp}.$$
Moreover $B/J$ is regular because $A/I$ is. The chart identifies $J$ with the ideal generated by nonunit sections of $N_{\bar y}$. Thus both local conditions in [def-trf-fs-log-blowup] hold at each geometric point, proving log regularity.

The finite-index chart inclusion gives $P=\{0\}$ if and only if $Q=\{0\}$: one direction is immediate, and in the other, $nq\in P$ forces $nq=0$, hence $q=0$, as follows: if $ng=0$ in the group completion, saturation puts both $g$ and $-g$ in the monoid, making $g$ a unit; sharpness forces $g=0$. Therefore the triviality of $N$ at $\bar y$ is equivalent to triviality of $M_D$ at a lift $\bar x$. The latter means $\bar x\notin E$ by [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. The invariant set $E$ is a union of orbits, so all lifts agree on this condition, and the triviality locus is exactly $V=Y\setminus q(E)$. Now apply [lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure] to $(Y,N)$, which is locally Noetherian fs log regular by Steps 1–4: $V$ is open dense and $N=\mathcal O_Y\cap j_*\mathcal O_V^\times$. Consequently $q(E)=Y\setminus V$ is closed, and [def-trf-log-regular-pair] says precisely that $(Y,q(E))$ is a log regular pair with the required divisorial structure.

proof_origin.place: Exposé VI, proof 3.7(a)–(c) and paragraph after 3.5; VI 1.4 for the pair.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q109-512a3bdf0 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item and the three new nodes in full, every cited statement, and ILO VI 1.1-1.8 and 3.1-3.7 (pp.69-76) plus Stacks 0BRH and 03BK. The item statement is unchanged: it is VI 3.2 without the Kummer-etale clause, in the pair form of VI 1.4. Generic freeness and integrality are inherited and unused, not weakened. Step 1: N is a log structure (elementary), and the strict-local child's hypotheses hold (Noetherian, finite surjective quotient, fs and G-stable M_D). Step 2: the pair definition and the equivariant-chart child (VI 3.5(a), true: H fixes the geometric point, so the cocycle can be corrected into mu_n because 1+m is uniquely n-divisible). Step 3: I checked every hypothesis of the local-Kummer child. That child is true: P^gp=L, P fs sharp by Gordan, M^H=P+B^x by reduction mod m, and B/J=A/I by the Reynolds operator plus Nakayama (I^H in J). Its etale-neighbourhood clause, from VI 3.5(b), is what makes N fs. Step 4: 00GK and 00OK give dim B=dim A; ranks agree because nQ^gp is in L; this gives log regularity. Step 5: P=0 iff Q=0 by saturation and sharpness; then lem-trf-log-regular-divisorial-structure gives the pair. Small cases tested: trivial H, rank 0, mu_n on x in k[x,y] (P=nN, B/J=A/I=k[y], 2=1+1); mu_2 acting by -1 is correctly excluded as not very tame. No duplicates: I read lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart, lem-trf-fine-log-stalk-chart-spreading, lem-a1-affine-groupoid-integral-invariants, lem-per-projective-finite-group-quotient and the parent. No child restates the item (D1). No SGA citation; steps under 2000 characters; proof_deps match the step citations. Accepted tool_uses: 00GK, 00OK, Niziol 2.6.
